pathophysiology.summary: Revascularisation restores blood flow past flow-limiting coronary stenoses by stenting (PCI) or bypass grafting (CABG). Its main purpose in stable angina is relieving symptoms (NICE CG126).
keyMechanisms: Fixed stenoses limit flow reserve and cause exertional ischaemia.
Complex multivessel or left main disease carries higher risk; CABG may improve survival in selected groups (NICE CG126).
Repeat revascularisation is less frequent after CABG than PCI (NICE CG126).

symptoms: Angina not controlled on optimal medical treatment.
physicalSigns: Often normal; signs of heart failure or valve disease.
redFlags: Rest or crescendo angina — manage as ACS

clinicalManagement.title: Indication
actions: Consider CABG or PCI when symptoms are not controlled on optimal medical treatment (NICE CG126 1.5.1).
Offer CABG when PCI is not appropriate, and PCI when CABG is not appropriate, with suitable anatomy.

clinicalManagement.title: PCI or CABG
actions: Weigh potential survival advantage of CABG in multivessel disease with diabetes, age over 65, or complex three-vessel/left main disease (NICE CG126 1.5.6).
Discuss left main or complex three-vessel disease at a multidisciplinary meeting with surgeons and interventional cardiologists (NICE CG126 1.5.8).
Give balanced information: both relieve symptoms; stroke is uncommon after either; repeat procedures fewer after CABG.

clinicalManagement.title: Pre-operative assessment
actions: Grade surgery (minor, intermediate, major/complex) and ASA status; order only the tests NICE NG45 lists for that combination.
Do not routinely order chest X-ray, urine dipstick, sickle tests or HbA1c in people without diabetes (NICE NG45).
Discuss stopping smoking and reducing alcohol; manage iron-deficiency anaemia (NICE NG180).
Make an individual anticoagulant plan if the person takes anticoagulants (NICE NG45).

clinicalManagement.title: VTE prophylaxis
actions: Cardiac surgery: consider mechanical prophylaxis and LMWH for at least 7 days if not otherwise anticoagulated (NICE NG89 1.15).

clinicalManagement.title: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (MOH Protocol-015)
actions: CABG: screen and decolonise MRSA; cefazolin 2 g IV (3 g if 120 kg or more) within 60 min (MOH p. 1).
Allergy: clindamycin 900 mg or vancomycin 15 mg/kg (max 2 g) (MOH p. 1).
Re-dose cefazolin every 4 h (or clindamycin every 6 h) if surgery lasts more than 4 h or blood loss exceeds 1,500 mL (MOH p. 1).
Stop prophylaxis within 24 h of the end of surgery, even with drains or catheters (MOH p. 4).
